minutes.headline: Committee cancelled the 8th-grade DC trip, approved a pre-K tuition rebate, and rescheduled the Galapagos trip.
minutes.summary: Remote meeting during the COVID closure. The committee approved a pre-K tuition adjustment for twelve families and voted on cancelling the eighth-grade trip, with debate over the non-refundable deposit. It rescheduled the Galapagos trip to next spring and heard remote learning presentations from the school administrators. The FY21 level service budget was mentioned; the budget hearing is set for April 29.

public_comment.topic: Urged the committee to push the travel agency hard to refund the non-refundable DC trip deposits.

what_happened.line: The committee approved a pre-K tuition price adjustment for a group of families, some of whom had already paid in full and need refunds.
A motion to cancel the eighth-grade trip was put to a vote, but the result is not audible in the recording, so the outcome is unconfirmed.
Administration is to try to get an accounting of the non-refundable deposit from the travel agent and include it in the letter to families.
The committee voted to reschedule the Galapagos trip to next April or June.
The next meeting was set as a budget hearing on April 29 at 7 o'clock.

why_it_matters: Families with children in pre-K or the eighth-grade trip are affected directly: one vote changes what they owe or are refunded, and the trip deposit may be only partly recoverable, with refunds taking weeks to months.
The FY21 level service budget and first-year state aid under the Student Opportunity Act were both unsettled, so the April 29 hearing is where residents can weigh in on next year's school spending.
